examples.text: Avoir, garder une main nue et l’autre gantée.
Vous êtes difficile à ganter. - Être bien ganté.
Des souliers qui gantent le pied bien cambré.
Il est préférable de se ganter pour sortir dans un tel froid.

glosses: Avoir une certaine pointure de gants.

examples.text: HANAË, off, fière : Je gante du huit et demi. KONRAD : Je le sais. J'ai assez baisé vos belles mains.

glosses: An item of clothing, covering all or part of the hand and fingers, but usually allowing independent movement of the fingers.

examples.text: I wore gloves to keep my hands warm.
The boxing champ laced on his gloves before the big bout.

glosses: The ability to catch a hit ball.

examples.text: Frederico had a great glove, but he couldn't hit a curveball, so he never broke into the pros.

glosses: A challenge from one to another.

examples.text: to throw down the glove, i.e. to offer a challenge; to take up the glove, to accept it

glosses: To catch the ball in a baseball mitt.

examples.text: He gloved the line drive for the third out.

glosses: To put a glove or gloves on.

examples.text: Maxwell gloved his hand so that he wouldn't leave fingerprints, then pulled the trigger.
After the maids had hatted and gloved the girls, the carriage was summoned and I was carted around one church after another.

glosses: To touch (a delivery) with one's glove while the gloved hand is on the bat. Under the rules of cricket, the batsman is deemed to have hit the ball.
